logic: Zero-crossing rate: high for fricatives/aspiration (the /s/ of 'yes', 'stop'), low for vowels/nasals.
Variation of ZCR in time: words that mix a fricative and a vowel ('yes', 'stop') vs. purely voiced ones ('no', 'down').
Spectral centroid: brightness; separates fricative/burst-rich words from low-formant words.
Centroid movement: formant glides (e.g. the diphthong in 'no', 'go').
85% spectral roll-off: where the energy ends (fricatives push it above 4 kHz).
Spectral bandwidth: spread of energy around the centroid (noise-like vs. harmonic).
Spectral flatness (log): noise-like (near 0 dB) vs. tonal/harmonic frames.
Spectral flux: frame-to-frame change; plosive bursts ('d' in 'down', 't' in 'stop', 'p' in 'up').
Energy < 1 kHz vs. > 4 kHz (dB): voiced vowel/nasal energy vs. fricative energy.
Slope of the long-term log spectrum: voice quality / channel colouring.
p95 - p10 of the frame level (dB) over valid frames: speech vs. steady noise (Phase-1 descriptor).
Share of valid frames within 35 dB of the loudest frame.
Duration of the active span (s): word length at the acoustic level, independent of padding.
Time of the first active frame (s): reaction/trim position; a recording-protocol cue, not content.
Energy-weighted time centre of the active span (0..1): early- vs. late-stressed words.
Number of local maxima of the smoothed energy envelope (syllable-count proxy).
